# pidginhost_server (Resource)

A cloud server.

Creation is asynchronous: the provider waits until the server's status is `active` and fails with a clear error if it becomes `failed`. The server ID is saved as soon as the API accepts the request, so a server that fails to provision is tainted and replaced on the next apply instead of being left behind.

Attributes marked *create-only* are sent when the server is created and cannot be changed afterwards; changing them replaces the server. The API never returns most of them, so after `terraform import` they can be added to the configuration without forcing a replacement.

Firewall rules, extra volumes, additional IPs and private network memberships have their own resources (`pidginhost_firewall_rule`, `pidginhost_volume`, `pidginhost_ipv4_attachment`, `pidginhost_private_network_attachment`). The create-only network and volume attributes here exist for the cases where the API needs them at creation time, such as booting with a public IP already attached.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pidginhost_ssh_key" "admin" {
  alias      = "admin"
  public_key = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
}

resource "pidginhost_firewall_rules_set" "web" {
  name = "web"
}

resource "pidginhost_server" "web" {
  hostname   = "web-1"
  image      = "ubuntu-24-04" # see the pidginhost_images data source
  package    = "cloud-s"      # see the pidginhost_server_packages data source
  ssh_key_id = pidginhost_ssh_key.admin.id
  new_ipv4   = true
  project    = "website"

  user_data = <<-EOT
    #!/bin/sh
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y nginx
  EOT

  # Applied before first boot; rules live in pidginhost_firewall_rule.
  firewall_rules_set_id = pidginhost_firewall_rules_set.web.id
  firewall_policy_in    = "DROP"

  destroy_protection = true
}

output "web_ipv4" {
  value = pidginhost_server.web.ipv4_address
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) *Create-only.* OS image, as a slug (recommended; see `pidginhost_images`) or ID. The API's name for the installed image is exported as `image_name`.
- `package` (String) Server package (plan), as a slug (recommended; see `pidginhost_server_packages`) or ID. Changing it resizes the server in place through the API's `modify-package` action; the provider waits until the server is `active` again.

### Optional

- `destroy_protection` (Boolean) Prevent the server from being destroyed. While `true`, `terraform destroy` fails; set it to `false` and apply before destroying. Defaults to `false`.
- `enable_ha` (Boolean) *Create-only.* Enable high availability (automatic restart and migration on node failure). Reflects the API's `ha_enabled`.
- `extra_volume_product` (String) *Create-only.* Storage product of an extra volume created with the server. Prefer `pidginhost_volume`, which can be resized and is tracked in state.
- `extra_volume_size` (Number) *Create-only.* Size in GB of the extra volume.
- `firewall_policy_in` (String) Default policy for inbound traffic not matched by a rule: `ACCEPT`, `DROP` or `REJECT`. The API default is `ACCEPT`. Can be changed in place.
- `firewall_policy_out` (String) Default policy for outbound traffic not matched by a rule: `ACCEPT`, `DROP` or `REJECT`. The API default is `ACCEPT`. Can be changed in place.
- `firewall_rules_set_id` (String) ID of the `pidginhost_firewall_rules_set` applied to the server's public interface. It is applied at creation, before first boot, and can be changed or removed in place.
- `generation` (String) *Create-only.* Hardware generation slug. When omitted, the API's default is used.
- `hostname` (String) Hostname. When omitted, the API picks one. Changing it replaces the server (the API cannot rename a server).
- `new_ipv4` (Boolean) *Create-only.* Allocate a new IPv4 and attach it before first boot. The address is not managed as a separate resource.
- `new_ipv6` (Boolean) *Create-only.* Allocate a new IPv6 and attach it before first boot.
- `no_network_acknowledged` (Boolean) *Create-only.* Confirm that the server is intentionally created without a public IP.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the default user. Can be changed in place. The API never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected. It is stored in the Terraform state.
- `power_state` (String) Desired power state: `running` or `stopped`. Stopping uses a graceful shutdown and falls back to a hard stop if the guest does not power off. When omitted, the power state is reported but not managed.
- `private_address` (String) *Create-only.* Address in `private_network_id`. Leave empty for automatic assignment.
- `private_network_id` (String) *Create-only.* ID of a private network to join at creation. Prefer `pidginhost_private_network_attachment`, which can be changed later; do not use both for the same network.
- `project` (String) Project label used to group resources in the control panel. Can be changed in place.
- `public_ipv4` (String) *Create-only.* ID or address of an IPv4 you already own (`pidginhost_ipv4`), attached before first boot.
- `public_ipv6` (String) *Create-only.* ID or address of an IPv6 you already own (`pidginhost_ipv6`), attached before first boot.
- `ssh_key_id` (String) *Create-only.* ID or fingerprint of a stored SSH key (`pidginhost_ssh_key`) to install.
- `ssh_public_key` (String) SSH public key for the default user. Can be changed in place, but **applying a new key regenerates cloud-init data and reboots a running server**. Setting it to `""` removes the key from future cloud-init data without revoking keys already in the guest.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user_data` (String) *Create-only.* Startup script run on first boot (cloud-init user data). The API documents it as an executable script with a shebang, such as `#!/bin/sh`. The API stores it in cleartext, so do not put secrets in it.

### Read-Only

- `cpus` (Number) Number of vCPUs.
- `disk_size` (Number) Boot disk size, as reported by the API.
- `id` (String) Server ID.
- `image_name` (String) The installed image, as reported by the API.
- `ipv4_address` (String) Primary public IPv4 address, if any.
- `ipv6_address` (String) Primary public IPv6 address, if any.
- `memory` (Number) Memory, as reported by the API.
- `private_networks` (Attributes List) Private network interfaces of the server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--private_networks))
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status reported by the API (`active`, `provisioning`, ...).
- `username` (String) Default login user.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--private_networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `private_networks`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) Address of the server in the network.
- `interface` (String) Interface name.
- `network` (String) Network, as reported by the API.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a server by its ID. Create-only attributes that the API does not
# return (image, user_data, password, ...) can then be added to the
# configuration without forcing a replacement.
terraform import pidginhost_server.web 123
```
